zema.how_to_read: Macro-F1 averages the three leakage states equally (1.0 is perfect; always guessing the most common state scores 0.19 to 0.24 here). Bars are 95% intervals over leakage runs. The chronological split is the honest one: it tests on later cycles than it trains on.
zema.contrast: Same model, same data: 1.000 on a random split, 0.476 on a chronological one
zema.scope_note: These results come from a hydraulic test rig (ZeMA). They do not transfer to centrifugal pumps, and no ZeMA model scores CIRA data.

calibration.text: very poor: top-label probabilities are off by 0.40 on average (ECE); Brier 0.875, worse than always predicting the class shares (0.709)

cira.how_to_read: Each mode is one detector revision on the same real days. Running time in a case is the share of the pump's running time inside an open review case: lower is quieter, but CIRA has no fault labels, so quieter is not proven better. The heat map shows how often a synthetic fault of each type and size was detected.

cira.key_finding: On real October data the pre-registered 3a-3 detector keeps 90.5% of pump B's and 55.9% of pump A's running time inside a review case, so a case means "look here", not "fault"; on synthetic injections, dropout and stuck faults are always detected, but a 6-sigma step only in 7 of 15.
cira.exploratory_note: Exploratory, outside the protocol: pump A with a 1 h minimum fit instead of the pre-registered 2 h, so that the across-day modes do not abstain on it (see the report).

assistant.how_to_read: The raw pass rate is how often the model's own answer passed the checker; the final pass rate counts what users saw, the checked answer or the evidence summary. Holdout questions were written and committed before each run. Checker revision 2 is the final one.

flagged.text: This system provides read-only condition monitoring information and cannot determine whether the pump should be stopped or started; that is an operational/safety decision outside the scope of this data review.
flagged.why: A refusal that names the decision it will not make; the rule reads "should be stopped" as directive phrasing.
